en.Les mots 会 (huì), 能 (néng), et 可以 (kěyǐ): Words 会 (Huì), 能 (neng), and 可以 (kěy) can be distinguished by their basic sense, deeper than simply "power":会 (huì) may mean "know how" and can be used to express something you can do because you have learned to do.能 (neng) means "to be able to" and expresses a certain natural ability to do something.可以 (kěy) means to "have permission from" or "to be allowed to" and means that something can be done with the consent of another person.
en.Les ordres négatifs en chinois (\"ne pas: Negative orders in Chinese ("do not" or "don't") are formed with 不要. The subject is most often omitted, as in French.

In other words, sentences in 把 must have an object that is "obvious". This implies that the object should be "defined" (often preceded by 'the/la/les' in French), or "generic". In passive sentences, the object of an action becomes the subject of the sentence and what was the topic of the phrase (active voice) becomes secondary (agent complement) and may or may not be added in the passive sentence.

en.Les questions interrogatives fermées en: The questions closed in Chinese can also be formulated with 不 (bù). This is done by adding an affirmative-negative structure at the end of the sentence.
en.Les questions rhétoriques sont utilisées: The rhetorical questions are used to express one's own opinion and often do not need an answer. A common rhetorical question in French is: "Are you completely stupid?" In Chinese, 难道 (nándào) is used as a marker to form this type of question.
en.Les structures négatives ajoutent simple: Negative structures simply add a 不 (bù) or 没 (mei) after 都 (dōu)/也 (yě) Instead of expressing "all" or "all", the meaning will be "none" or "more at all".
en.Les sujets des deux \"évènements\" peuve: The subjects of the two "events" may be the same, but it's not necessary. If they were the same, then you don't need to repeat it.
en.Les traductions \"dans le futur\", \"à l: Translations "in the future", "in the future", "one of these days" or "later" can be used for 以后 (y-h-u).

en.Les verbes associés à 着 sont en général: The verbs associated with 着 In general, state verbs. Unlike action verbs, you describe an action that is content to be there. It can be standing, lying down, sitting, hanging... the essential thing is that no energy is spent doing anything.
en.Les verbes causatifs sont des verbes pou: Causative verbs are verbs that push people to do things. These verbs are in French "faire", "avoir" et "pronrà", as in "bringe la soup à Jean". In Chinese the most common causal verbs are: 让 (ràng) 叫 (Jiao) 使 (sh) 请 Be careful to take note of the different senses and levels of politeness. 使 (sh) 让 (ràng) when used with causal verbs have the same meaning (doing) but 使 (sh) is used either formally or in writing while 让 (ràng) is more present in the oral.
en.Les verbes et classificateurs sont souve: Verbs and classifiers are often used in phrases 把 and are placed at the end of the sentence.
en.Les verbes peuvent prendre des complémen: Verbs may take potentiality supplements indicating whether the action is or is not possible, if something "can" or "can't" happen. They are particularly useful in Chinese to explain the context surrounding an action.
en.Les verbes séparables en chinois existen: The separable verbs in Chinese also exist in French: they are verbal sentences (or compound verbs). While the structure of the verbal phrases is different in French, the "separable" qualifier works in the same way. Let's take the verb "let it turn" for example: Let my new computer run. Let my new computer spin. In French, the verb "let it rotate" can separate its two parts (a verb and a preposition), and other words may be placed between them. Separatable verbs in Chinese work in the same manner, except that both parties are a verb and an object (name).Let us take a typical example of the Chinese language by using the verb 见面 which means "to meet."
en.Les verbes séparés font partie de ces ch: Separate verbs are part of these things that you can never avoid. Many extremely common verbs like "to lie down" (睡觉) or "meeting" (见面) are separable verbs, and unless you learn which verbs are separable and how they work, you will make the same mistakes every time, even in your simplest sentences.
en.Les verbes 说, 跟 et 对 peuvent être utilis: Verbs 说, 跟 and 对 can be used in similar structures. 跟 and 对 are prepositions, and can express the fact that one person speaks to another person.
en.Lier des actions ensemble en chinois est: Linking actions together in Chinese is very simple. There is no new word or sentence needed to learn.
en.Littéralement \"dix mille pour un\", 万一: Literally "ten thousand for one," 万一 (wànyī) is a word used to evoke unlikely possibilities, in the sense of "and if", "in case" or "in the unlikely event where". It is most often used to evoke unfortunate situations.
en.Littéralement cela veut dire \"Quel est: Literally this means "What is your honourable name?". Use this form only to indicate extreme politeness. Related keywords: 姓
en.Littéralement, 以内 et 以外 signifient \"à l: Literally 以内 and 以外 This spatial sense can extend to all kinds of abstract meanings, as you will see below. Note that 以外 often combines with 除了.
en.Littéralement, 够了 signifie \"c'est assez: Literally 够了 "It's enough." When anyone who speaks has it over his head to do something, or he is out of control, 够了 can be placed behind a small number of verbs.Some common examples:
en.Littéralement, 通过 peut également permett: Literally 通过 can also express the fact of "passing through (a legal, administrative system, ...)" in order to arrive at a recognition, solution or agreement.
en.Logiquement, 差点没 n'est pas si différent: Logically, 差点没 is not so different from 差点. In fact, you should not think about it as a single word; think of the 没 as follows: 差点 Yet its use can be a little confusing and is worth examining more closely.
en.Lors d'une utilisation avec un nom, plac: When using a name, place 正好 right after the name, followed by an adjective.
en.Lors de l'apparition de mots temporels a: When time words appear before or after the subject, you can also add Time + 的时候 (of shíhou) after the subject.
en.Lors de la spécification de quantités (e: When specifying quantities (and using a classifier to do so), 两 It is used to express "two unit or entity of something" or "both". Here are some examples of the use of 两 (li)ng:
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé avec des activités: When used with activities that have been learned or studied 能 (neng) often means that the present circumstances allow or do not permit an execution of the action. In other words, "this is possible" or "it is not possible". Sometimes it is a little exaggerated and has only as meaning "that's permitted" or "that's not allowed"; in these latter cases 可以 (kěy) can be used to replace 能 (Neng)
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé avec un adjectif,: When used with an adjective, he often has an adverb in front of him, like "很, 非常, 这么, 那么" etc.
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé avec un verbe, 正好: When used with a verb, 正好 Right in front.
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé avec 得 (ou 不) 住 fo: When used with 得 (or 不) 住 works as a complement of potentiality , and indicates that someone's skills are sufficient (or not) for the current task.
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé avec 得 (ou 不), 着 p: When used with 得 (or 不), 着 It is a potential complement, and indicates that someone has the (or not) ability to deal with the current problem.
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé comme complément d: When used as an additional result, 住 (zhù) may mean "stop" or "close". It can also be used as a complement to potentiality, meaning then "to be capable of".
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé comme complément r: When used as a resultant supplement, 着 (zháo) expresses the fact that an action has come to its end or resulted in something else. It can be used in Chinese as a complement of potentiality, meaning "being capable of".
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé comme préposition,: When used as a preposition, "向" indicates that an action has been made to a point, but is not a real movement towards this point. A good example in French would be "it looks at the window". There is indeed no real move.
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé comme verbe, il ex: When used as a verb, it expresses the fact that the speaker does not blame anyone for the situation he is describing.
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé de cette manière,: When used in this way, 了(the) is placed at the end of the sentence to express that this is a new situation.
When used in this way, 啊 (a) is placed at the end of the sentence and gives a nuance of exclamation, excitement or enthusiasm.
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé de la sorte, le lo: When used in this way, the speaker does not blame anyone for the situation described; sometimes the person who does not deserve a reprimand will be directly mentioned after 难怪, as in the first two examples. However, often the context suggests who is the person in question and it is no longer necessary to mention it, as in the last three examples. Related keywords: 难怪, 怪不得, 原来, 这也难怪
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé en tant que modifi: When used as an attribution modifier, it usually moves after the verb and you will always need to add a 的.
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé littéralement, 出（来: When used literally, 出（来） is rather intuitive and means "come out of" (in the direction of speaker):
en.Lorsqu'il est utilisé pour indiquer des: When used to indicate places, 在 (zài) is usually placed immediately after the subject. However, there are some exceptions to this rule. In certain cases, the usual rule of the place preceding the verb does not apply: the place is placed after the verb. This often happens with particular verbs such as: 住 (zhù), 放 (fàng), 坐 (zuò) or 站 (zhàn).
en.Lorsqu'il faut faire face à un choix, 不如: When faced with a choice, 不如 can also be used to mean "could also" to reinforce the idea that one of the two choices is better than the other. When it is used in this way, it has the same meaning as 不妨.
en.Lorsqu'il n'y a qu'un seul sujet avec 不但: When there is only one subject with 不但的而且The subject must be placed at the beginning of the sentence, before 不但 and 而且. When using two different subjects, you must place the first behind 不但 and the second back 而且.
en.Lorsqu'il s'agit de rendre un adjectif n: When it comes to making a negative adjective in Chinese, one uses 不 (bù).
en.Lorsqu'il vous est posé une question sou: When you are asked a question in this form, there are two expected answers: Option A or Option B. You could answer something else, but usually the question being asked to you in that way, your interlocutor expects you to respond by choosing one of the two options. For example, if you are asked whether you prefer coffee or tea, most people will answer either, but not both. 还是 (háishì) is used in Chinese to form questions offering two possibilities.
en.Lorsqu'on veut exprimer \"faire quelque: When you want to express "do something as you mean" in Chinese, the structure can be used. "想 + verb + 就 + verb".
en.Lorsqu'un adjectif indique un changement: When an adjective indicates a change in the subject, 了 (the) is placed at the end of the sentence to mark this status change.
en.Lorsque ce qui suit 还是 est un verbe à la: When the following 还是 is a verb in the negative form, 吧 of the end is not mandatory.
en.Lorsque diverses choses sont 差不多 (chàbùd: When various things are 差不多 (chàbùduō), this means that they are "more or less the same / identical / similar." (The part meaning "the same" is implicit in Chinese.)
en.Lorsque l'on parle d'un point de vue, vo: When you talk from a point of view, you can just say 看来 then give your vision of things.
en.Lorsque vous avez besoin d'utiliser 以来 d: When you need to use 以来 in a more formal or written context, you can add before the time period or event 自, 从 or 自从 (or other similar words).
en.Lorsque vous exprimez que quelque chose: When you express that something is not worth it, you can either say 不值得 either 值不得. Associated keywords: 值得, 不值得, 值不得
en.Lorsque vous faites suivre 从来 (cónglái): When you make it follow 从来 (cónglái) 不 (bù), you express the fact that you have never done anything (as a habit or as a rule). It is often used to refuse something like in "I never drink".
en.Lorsque vous l'utilisez avec un adjectif: When you use it with an adjective, 不怎么 becomes similar to 不太, which means that the degree of your adjective will not be very high.
en.Lorsque vous parlez de différents aspect: When you talk about different aspects of a situation in Chinese, "一方面的，(另)一方面"" (yī fāngmiàn..., (lìng) yī fāngmiàn ...) can be used in a way similar to "On the one hand..., on the other..." or "on the other..." in French.
en.Lorsque vous parlez de la quantité de qu: When you talk about the amount of something in Chinese, you need to use a classifier.
en.Lorsque vous parlez en chinois avec quel: When you speak in Chinese with someone about something that happened, 以后 (y-h-u) and 的时候 (of shíhou) are often used. They can both translate into "when" but their meaning is different.
en.Lorsque vous posez une question, 还是 peut: When you ask a question, 还是 can be used to offer a choice or option.
en.Lorsque vous répondez à une question fer: When you answer a closed question using 去 (qù), you do not need to have it precede anything. However, it is important to note that you cannot use 去 (qù) without any context.
en.Lorsque vous souhaitez impliquer en chin: When you want to imply in Chinese that something is reasonably correct, it is possible to use 还 (hái) just in front of the positive adjectives.
en.Lorsque vous utilisez des mots temporels: When you use time words such as "Yesterday", "Tomorrow", "This Week", etc., in a sentence it is extremely important to use the correct order of Chinese words.
en.Lorsque vous utilisez 不怎么 (bù zěnme) ava: When you use 不怎么 (bù zěnme) before an adjective in Chinese, it means "not very" or "not so much". This structure is similar to the French-speaking structure when we say for example "not very good".
en.Lorsque vous utilisez 差不多 (chàbùduō) com: When you use 差不多 (chàbùduō) as adverb, place it in front of the adjective or verb.
en.Lorsque 不怎么 est utilisé avec un verbe, i: Where 不怎么 is used with a verb, it means that someone does not put enough of his to do something. In other words, the action is "not often" done. When the verb is used with an object, it also means that the number (or quantity) is very small.
en.Lorsque 吧 (ba) est utilisé dans une phra: Where 吧 (ba) is used in a sentence, it is used in Chinese to list two options that are given by the interlocutor. This gives the phrase a feeling of indecision and whose speaker does not know the rest. This construction has a negative connotation, because the options are not ideal.
en.Lorsque 对 est une préposition, il pointe: Where 对 is a preposition, it points to a particular target since it means "point towards" or "to". 跟 can only be used with 说.
en.Lorsque 对于 et 关于 agissent comme clauses: Where 对于 and 关于 act as adverbial clauses (a group of linked words that function as an adverb), they find themselves following different word orders. 对于 is placed before or after the subject, while 关于 can only be placed before the subject.
en.Lorsque 平常 est utilisé comme adjectif, i: Where 平常 is used as an adjective, it expresses the meaning of "common" or "banal". 平时 cannot be used in this way.
en.Lorsque 平时 est utilisé comme un nom, il: Where 平时 is used as a name, it is very similar to 平常 (used as a name).
en.Là encore, ce sont normalement des verbe: Here again, it is normally verbs or verbal groups that follow each 越, but adjectives are also possible (usually after the second 越).
en.Là encore, des mots comme 仅仅，只，就，才 sont: Here again, words like 仅仅，只，就，才 are optional and add insistence.
en.Là encore, vous pourriez employer 和 (hé): Again, you could use 和 (he) instead of 跟 (g(9)n), but 跟 (gюn) is more common.

en.Même si vous avez bien compris que 了 ne: Even if you have understood that 了 Do not mark the "past" in Chinese, you may use it by mistake. Imagine for example that you wanted to ask a question about a past event: would you say one of the following phrases?
en.N'employez pas 互相 (hùxiāng) avec un verb: Don't use 互相 (hùxiāng) with a verb of only one syllable. If you really want to use it, lengthen the verb by adding an accuracy after it.
en.N'oubliez pas d'ajouter le 了 puisqu'il s: Don't forget to add the 了 since this is a sort of exclaiming statement as 太好了. Your sentence would be false without this one.
en.N'oubliez pas d'ajouter 都 !: Don't forget to add 都 - I'm sorry.
en.N'oubliez pas qu'il s'agit d'une excepti: Remember that this is an exception to the rule. A common error is to overuse this structure, creating incorrect sentences. Note the following correct and incorrect versions to better understand:
Do not use 不 (bù) 有 (Yu).
en.Ne pas oublier qu'en plus, et il y a tou: Do not forget that besides, and there are all kinds of other ways to express "and" like words [并]]], 并且, 还有 or structures 又......又...... and 既......又.......The following sentences do not follow the above rules and are therefore not correct phrases.
en.Note importante : que ce soit pour 除了 ou: Important note: be it for 除了 or 以外 (generally it will be 以外), it is possible to remove them from the sentence without changing its meaning.
en.Note: La structure \"AABB\" pour le redo: Note: The structure "AABB" for the repetition of adjectives in two syllables contrasts with the structure "ABAB" for the doubling of verbs into two syllables. Related keywords: 的, 地, 一下
en.Notez aussi que 一直 (yīzhí) signifie \"en: Note also that 一直 (yīzhí) means "continuously" and is often more naturally translated as "always" in the French version.
en.Notez qu'avec certains verbes qui sont d: Note that with some verbs which are already "reciprocal" by nature, 互相 (hùxiāng) duplicates and becomes useless. The following turns are therefore not wrong, but a little strange.
en.Notez qu'avec le sujet \"nous\", cela re: Note that with the subject "we", it amounts to saying "Let's go (do something)". 吧 (ba) makes the suggestion look more polite and tempting.
en.Notez qu'en français nous n'utilisons pa: Note that in French we do not use the word "less". For example, instead of saying "wood less water", we would tend to say "don't drink so much water." In Chinese, on the other hand, using 少 Avoiding a negative command (to tell someone not to "do" something) is also a subtle way of not looking haughty and disdainful.
en.Notez qu'en français, on peut très bien: Note that in French, you can very well ask "is it near here?" when the distance is obviously short. In Chinese, you always ask "Is it far from here?".
en.Notez qu'en niant une construction 是⋯⋯的,: Note that by denying a building 是的的the action was actually taken, and only the detail highlighted by 是的的 In the second sentence, we understand that 他 didn't go there with 我们But he went well with someone. 是的的 So negative would be wonderful in the last scenes of a police series.
en.Notez qu'ici le caractère 了 se prononce: Note that here the character 了 Is pronounced "li-o".
en.Notez qu'ici le caractère 着 se prononce: Note that here the character 着 pronounces "zháo".
en.Notez qu'il est parfois difficile de ren: Note that it is sometimes difficult to render 竟然 (jìngrán) by a correct French word. It is sometimes a simple shade that goes wrong if one does not hear the tone of the voice.
en.Notez qu'il est préférable de placer 恐怕: Note that it is better to place 恐怕 before the subject of the sentence.
en.Notez qu'il n'est pas nécessaire d'ajout: Note that it is not necessary to add 的 Here. Examples
en.Notez qu'il ne faut employer ni le verbe: Note that neither the verb should be used 是 (shì), nor a classifier as 个 (gè) in these sentences.
en.Notez qu'il ne s'agit pas d'une relation: Note that this is not a unique relationship between names and classifiers. The same classifier can be used with different names:
en.Notez qu'on emploie 不是, et non simplemen: Note that we use 不是, and not just 不To deny 所有.
en.Notez qu'une autre manière courante d'ex: Note that another common way to express "also" is the word 也 (yě). What's the difference? 还 (hái), ONE subject does TWO different things, while with 也 (yě), TWO subjects do ONE thing.It is the difference between these two sentences in French: He prepared dinner and he also made dishes. She also did the dishes. If you translated those phrases into Chinese, the first (one topic, two actions) would take 还 (hái), and the second (a second topic, no new action) would take 也 (yě) Let's do it!
en.Notez que \"Verbe + 得\" peut aussi se pl: Note that "Verbe + 得" may also be placed before 不比.
en.Notez que \"还是\" ou \"就是\" sert souvent: Note that "还是" or "就是" is often used to point out that in the end, nothing has changed.
en.Notez que c'est la structure \"Adj. + 地: Note that this is the structure "Adj. + 地 (de)" that turns the adjective into "adverbial phrase". If you use an adverb directly (instead of an adjective), then you do not need to add it at all 地 (de).
en.Notez que certains mots n'ont pas besoin: Note that some words do not need classifiers because they are themselves measuring words. For example: 天 (tiān), 年 (nián), 周 (zhōu), 次 (cì), etc.
en.Notez que certains noms peuvent former d: Note that some names can form ordinals without 第 (dì):
Note that this job is limited.
en.Notez que cette forme n'est pas une faço: Note that this form is not a way to add a comparison to an adjective or be the substitute for 比 For each case, you add "even more" to an already existing "amount", as in: "I am already rich but I want to be even more rich."
en.Notez que cette structure de phrase est: Note that this sentence structure is the inverse of construction 更不用说.
en.Notez que cette structure est identique: Note that this structure is identical to the repetition of verbs in a syllable.
en.Notez que cette structure est un complém: Note that this structure is a qualifier supplement (called 程度补语 in Chinese), and one of the few who do not need to add 得.
en.Notez que chacune de ces phrases porte u: Note that each of these sentences carries an idea of urgency, even when the word 现在 This is why an implied "now" has been added in some French translations.
en.Notez que dans ces exemples l'objet est: Note that in these examples the object is introduced first with the subject.In the end, please take into account that this structure is nothing more than a combination of the expression of a finished action with "the" and the structure for questions in "ma". 了吗

zh.Lorsque vous utilisez 差不多 (chàbùduō) com: 使用时 差不多 (chàbúdu ⁇ )作为副词,放在形容词或动词前.
zh.Lorsque 不怎么 est utilisé avec un verbe, i: 在哪里 不怎么 用动词,它意味着某人没有把足够的时间来做某事。换句话说,动作是“不经常”完成的。当动词用一个对象时,它也意味着数字(或数量)非常小。
zh.Lorsque 吧 (ba) est utilisé dans une phra: 在哪里 吧 (ba)在句子中被用到,中文中用于列出对话者给出的两个选项。这让该短语有一种不决感,而其演讲者不知道其他的选项。这一构思带有负面含义,因为选项并不理想。
zh.Lorsque 对 est une préposition, il pointe: 在哪里 对 它指向特定的目标,因为它的意思是"指向"或"去". 跟 只能用于 说。 。 。 。
zh.Lorsque 对于 et 关于 agissent comme clauses: 在哪里 对于 财务报告和审定财务报表 关于 它们作为附加条款(一组具有副词功能的链接词),它们发现自己遵循不同的单词顺序。 对于 放在主体之前或之后,同时 关于 只能放在主体之前。
zh.Lorsque 平常 est utilisé comme adjectif, i: 在哪里 平常 被作为形容词使用,它表达了"通俗"或"banal"的含义. 平时 无法以这种方式使用 。
zh.Lorsque 平时 est utilisé comme un nom, il: 在哪里 平时 用作名称,它与 平常 (用作名相.
zh.Là encore, ce sont normalement des verbe: 这里,通常都是动词或口头组合 越,但形容词也可以(通常在第二个之后) 越) (中文(简体) ).
zh.Là encore, des mots comme 仅仅，只，就，才 sont: 再说一遍,这些话... 仅仅，只，就，才 是可选的,并加上坚持。
zh.Là encore, vous pourriez employer 和 (hé): 再说一遍,你用得着 和 (他) 而不是(他) 跟 (g(9)n),但是, 跟 (g ⁇ n)比较常见.
